## Hypergeometric Test

```{r}
# Hypergeometric test for enrichment of mutations in deceased patients
# Create binary variables for mutation status and survival outcome
df$has_mutation <- ifelse(df$group %in% c(paste0(GENE, "_mut"), "LLM_oncogenic"), 1, 0)
df$deceased <- df$OS_STATUS

# Create contingency table
# Rows: deceased (1) vs alive (0)
# Cols: mutation (1) vs no mutation (0)
contingency_table <- table(df$deceased, df$has_mutation)
print("Contingency Table (Deceased vs Mutation Status):")
print(contingency_table)

# Hypergeometric test parameters
# q = number of deceased patients with mutations - 1
# m = total number of patients with mutations
# n = total number of patients without mutations
# k = total number of deceased patients

if (sum(df$has_mutation) > 0 && sum(df$deceased) > 0) {
  deceased_with_mut <- sum(df$deceased == 1 & df$has_mutation == 1)
  total_with_mut <- sum(df$has_mutation == 1)
  total_without_mut <- sum(df$has_mutation == 0)
  total_deceased <- sum(df$deceased == 1)

  # Hypergeometric test (upper tail - testing for over-representation)
  hyper_pval <- phyper(deceased_with_mut - 1,
                       total_with_mut,
                       total_without_mut,
                       total_deceased,
                       lower.tail = FALSE)

  cat("\nHypergeometric Test Results:\n")
  cat(sprintf("Deceased with mutation: %d\n", deceased_with_mut))
  cat(sprintf("Total with mutation: %d\n", total_with_mut))
  cat(sprintf("Total without mutation: %d\n", total_without_mut))
  cat(sprintf("Total deceased: %d\n", total_deceased))
  cat(sprintf("P-value (enrichment): %.4e\n", hyper_pval))

  # Fisher's exact test as alternative (two-sided)
  fisher_result <- fisher.test(contingency_table)
  cat(sprintf("\nFisher's Exact Test P-value: %.4e\n", fisher_result$p.value))
  cat(sprintf("Odds Ratio: %.4f\n", fisher_result$estimate))
} else {
  cat("\nInsufficient data for hypergeometric test\n")
}
```

## Cox Proportional Hazards Model

```{r}
# Cox proportional hazards model
cox_model <- coxph(Surv(OS_MONTHS, OS_STATUS) ~ group, data = df)

cat("\n=== Cox Proportional Hazards Model ===\n")
print(summary(cox_model))

# Extract hazard ratios with confidence intervals
cox_summary <- summary(cox_model)
hr_table <- data.frame(
  Group = rownames(cox_summary$conf.int),
  HR = cox_summary$conf.int[, "exp(coef)"],
  Lower_95 = cox_summary$conf.int[, "lower .95"],
  Upper_95 = cox_summary$conf.int[, "upper .95"],
  P_value = cox_summary$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
)

cat("\nHazard Ratios (reference: no_mutation):\n")
print(hr_table)

# Test proportional hazards assumption
cat("\n=== Test of Proportional Hazards Assumption ===\n")
ph_test <- cox.zph(cox_model)
print(ph_test)

# Log-rank test
cat("\n=== Log-rank Test ===\n")
logrank_test <- survdiff(Surv(OS_MONTHS, OS_STATUS) ~ group, data = df)
print(logrank_test)
cat(sprintf("\nLog-rank P-value: %.4e\n",
            pchisq(logrank_test$chisq,
                   length(logrank_test$n) - 1,
                   lower.tail = FALSE)))
```

### Pairwise Comparisons

```{r}
# Pairwise log-rank tests
cat("\n=== Pairwise Log-rank Tests ===\n")
group_levels <- levels(df$group)
n_groups <- length(group_levels)

# Create matrix to store p-values
pairwise_matrix <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_groups, ncol = n_groups)
rownames(pairwise_matrix) <- group_levels
colnames(pairwise_matrix) <- group_levels

# Perform pairwise comparisons
for (i in 1:(n_groups-1)) {
  for (j in (i+1):n_groups) {
    # Subset data for these two groups
    subset_data <- df[df$group %in% c(group_levels[i], group_levels[j]), ]
    subset_data$group <- droplevels(subset_data$group)

    # Perform log-rank test
    pairwise_test <- survdiff(Surv(OS_MONTHS, OS_STATUS) ~ group, data = subset_data)
    pval <- pchisq(pairwise_test$chisq, df = 1, lower.tail = FALSE)

    # Store in matrix
    pairwise_matrix[i, j] <- pval
    pairwise_matrix[j, i] <- pval

    cat(sprintf("%s vs %s: p = %.4e\n", group_levels[i], group_levels[j], pval))
  }
}

# Pairwise Cox models
cat("\n=== Pairwise Cox Model Comparisons ===\n")
pairwise_hr_matrix <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_groups, ncol = n_groups)
pairwise_hr_lower <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_groups, ncol = n_groups)
pairwise_hr_upper <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_groups, ncol = n_groups)
pairwise_cox_pval <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_groups, ncol = n_groups)
rownames(pairwise_hr_matrix) <- group_levels
colnames(pairwise_hr_matrix) <- group_levels
rownames(pairwise_hr_lower) <- group_levels
colnames(pairwise_hr_lower) <- group_levels
rownames(pairwise_hr_upper) <- group_levels
colnames(pairwise_hr_upper) <- group_levels
rownames(pairwise_cox_pval) <- group_levels
colnames(pairwise_cox_pval) <- group_levels

for (i in 1:(n_groups-1)) {
  for (j in (i+1):n_groups) {
    # Subset data for these two groups
    subset_data <- df[df$group %in% c(group_levels[i], group_levels[j]), ]
    subset_data$group <- droplevels(subset_data$group)

    # Perform Cox regression
    cox_pair <- coxph(Surv(OS_MONTHS, OS_STATUS) ~ group, data = subset_data)
    cox_summ <- summary(cox_pair)

    hr <- exp(coef(cox_pair))
    hr_lower <- cox_summ$conf.int[, "lower .95"]
    hr_upper <- cox_summ$conf.int[, "upper .95"]
    pval <- cox_summ$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"]

    # Store HRs (j vs i, so row i has higher hazard)
    pairwise_hr_matrix[i, j] <- hr
    pairwise_hr_matrix[j, i] <- 1/hr  # Reciprocal for opposite comparison

    pairwise_hr_lower[i, j] <- hr_lower
    pairwise_hr_upper[i, j] <- hr_upper
    pairwise_hr_lower[j, i] <- 1/hr_upper
    pairwise_hr_upper[j, i] <- 1/hr_lower

    pairwise_cox_pval[i, j] <- pval
    pairwise_cox_pval[j, i] <- pval

    cat(sprintf("%s vs %s: HR = %.2f (%.2f-%.2f), p = %.4e\n",
                group_levels[j], group_levels[i], hr, hr_lower, hr_upper, pval))
  }
}
```

### Pairwise Comparison Heatmap

```{r}
# Create heatmap of pairwise p-values
pdf(paste0("./pairwise_logrank_", GENE, ".pdf"), width=10, height=9)

par(mar = c(8, 8, 4, 6))

# Create color palette (white = not significant, red = significant)
color_breaks <- c(0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1)
colors <- c("darkred", "red", "orange", "yellow")

# Create matrix for plotting (log transform for better visualization)
plot_matrix <- -log10(pairwise_matrix)
diag(plot_matrix) <- NA

# Create the heatmap
image(1:n_groups, 1:n_groups, plot_matrix,
      col = heat.colors(20, rev = TRUE),
      xlab = "", ylab = "",
      main = paste("Pairwise Log-rank Test P-values -", GENE, "\n(-log10 scale)"),
      axes = FALSE,
      cex.main = 1.6)

# Add grid
abline(h = 0.5:(n_groups+0.5), col = "gray30", lwd = 0.5)
abline(v = 0.5:(n_groups+0.5), col = "gray30", lwd = 0.5)

# Add axis labels
axis(1, at = 1:n_groups, labels = group_levels, las = 2, cex.axis = 1.2)
axis(2, at = 1:n_groups, labels = group_levels, las = 2, cex.axis = 1.2)

# Add p-values as text
for (i in 1:n_groups) {
  for (j in 1:n_groups) {
    if (i != j && !is.na(pairwise_matrix[i, j])) {
      pval <- pairwise_matrix[i, j]
      text_color <- ifelse(pval < 0.05, "white", "black")

      # Format p-value
      if (pval < 0.001) {
        pval_text <- sprintf("%.1e", pval)
      } else {
        pval_text <- sprintf("%.3f", pval)
      }

      text(j, i, pval_text, cex = 1.0, col = text_color, font = 2)
    }
  }
}

# Add color legend
legend_x <- n_groups + 0.8
legend_y <- seq(1, n_groups, length.out = 5)
legend_labels <- c("< 0.001", "< 0.01", "< 0.05", "≥ 0.05")

legend("right",
       legend = c("p < 0.001", "p < 0.01", "p < 0.05", "p ≥ 0.05"),
       fill = c("darkred", "red", "orange", "yellow"),
       title = "Significance",
       cex = 1.1,
       xpd = TRUE,
       inset = c(-0.2, 0))

dev.off()
cat("Pairwise comparison heatmap saved to:", paste0("./pairwise_logrank_", GENE, ".pdf\n"))
```

### Combined Pairwise HR and P-value Heatmap

```{r}
# Create combined heatmap showing both HRs and p-values
pdf(paste0("./pairwise_combined_", GENE, ".pdf"), width=12, height=10)

par(mar = c(8, 8, 4, 2))

# Create color scale based on HR values
# HR < 1 (protective) = blue, HR = 1 (no effect) = white, HR > 1 (risk) = red
hr_for_color <- log2(pairwise_hr_matrix)
hr_for_color[is.na(hr_for_color)] <- 0
diag(hr_for_color) <- 0

# Color palette: blue for protective, white for neutral, red for increased risk
color_ramp <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100)
hr_range <- max(abs(hr_for_color), na.rm = TRUE)
color_breaks <- seq(-hr_range, hr_range, length.out = 101)

# Create the heatmap
image(1:n_groups, 1:n_groups, t(hr_for_color),
      col = color_ramp,
      xlab = "", ylab = "",
      main = paste("Pairwise Hazard Ratios with P-values -", GENE, "\n(Row vs Column)"),
      axes = FALSE,
      cex.main = 1.6,
      zlim = c(-hr_range, hr_range))

# Add grid
abline(h = 0.5:(n_groups+0.5), col = "gray30", lwd = 1)
abline(v = 0.5:(n_groups+0.5), col = "gray30", lwd = 1)

# Add axis labels
axis(1, at = 1:n_groups, labels = group_levels, las = 2, cex.axis = 1.3)
axis(2, at = 1:n_groups, labels = group_levels, las = 2, cex.axis = 1.3)

# Add HR values and p-values as text
for (i in 1:n_groups) {
  for (j in 1:n_groups) {
    if (i != j && !is.na(pairwise_hr_matrix[i, j])) {
      hr <- pairwise_hr_matrix[i, j]
      hr_low <- pairwise_hr_lower[i, j]
      hr_up <- pairwise_hr_upper[i, j]
      pval <- pairwise_cox_pval[i, j]

      # Determine text color based on background
      bg_color_intensity <- abs(hr_for_color[j, i])
      text_color <- ifelse(bg_color_intensity > 0.5, "white", "black")

      # Format text: HR on top, p-value below
      # HR text
      hr_text <- sprintf("HR=%.2f", hr)
      text(j, i + 0.15, hr_text, cex = 1.1, col = text_color, font = 2)

      # CI text
      ci_text <- sprintf("(%.2f-%.2f)", hr_low, hr_up)
      text(j, i, ci_text, cex = 0.9, col = text_color)

      # P-value text with significance markers
      if (pval < 0.001) {
        pval_text <- "p<0.001***"
      } else if (pval < 0.01) {
        pval_text <- sprintf("p=%.3f**", pval)
      } else if (pval < 0.05) {
        pval_text <- sprintf("p=%.3f*", pval)
      } else {
        pval_text <- sprintf("p=%.3f", pval)
      }
      text(j, i - 0.15, pval_text, cex = 0.85, col = text_color)
    }
  }
}

# Add diagonal labels
for (i in 1:n_groups) {
  text(i, i, "—", cex = 2, col = "gray50")
}

# Add legend for colors
legend_x <- n_groups * 1.15
legend_y_vals <- seq(1, n_groups, length.out = 5)
legend("right",
       legend = c("HR > 2 (Increased risk)",
                  "HR = 1 (No effect)",
                  "HR < 0.5 (Protective)"),
       fill = c("red", "white", "blue"),
       title = "Hazard Ratio",
       cex = 1.1,
       xpd = TRUE)

# Add note about significance
mtext("*, **, *** indicate p<0.05, p<0.01, p<0.001", side = 1, line = 7, cex = 0.9)

dev.off()
cat("Combined pairwise heatmap saved to:", paste0("./pairwise_combined_", GENE, ".pdf\n"))
```

### Cox Model Forest Plot

```{r}
# Create forest plot for Cox model hazard ratios
pdf(paste0("./cox_survival_", GENE, ".pdf"), width=14, height=10)

par(mar = c(6, 14, 5, 10))

# Get HR data
hrs <- hr_table$HR
lower <- hr_table$Lower_95
upper <- hr_table$Upper_95
pvals <- hr_table$P_value
group_names <- gsub("group", "", hr_table$Group)

# Create plot
n_groups <- nrow(hr_table)
y_pos <- n_groups:1

# Calculate better x-axis limits
x_min <- min(c(0.5, lower*0.9))
x_max <- max(c(2.5, upper*1.1))

# Set up plot area with more space
plot(1, type="n",
     xlim=c(x_min, x_max),
     ylim=c(0.3, n_groups + 0.7),
     xlab="Hazard Ratio (95% CI)",
     ylab="",
     main=paste("Cox Proportional Hazards Model -", GENE, "\n(Reference: no_mutation)"),
     yaxt="n",
     log="x",
     cex.lab=1.8,
     cex.main=2.0,
     cex.axis=1.6)

# Add vertical line at HR = 1
abline(v=1, lty=2, col="gray60", lwd=3)

# Add points and error bars
for (i in 1:n_groups) {
  # Error bars
  arrows(lower[i], y_pos[i], upper[i], y_pos[i],
         angle=90, code=3, length=0.1, lwd=3, col="darkblue")

  # Points
  points(hrs[i], y_pos[i], pch=18, cex=3.5, col="darkred")
}

# Add group labels on the left with larger font
axis(2, at=y_pos, labels=group_names, las=1, cex.axis=1.8)

# Add HR values and p-values on the right side, positioned better
for (i in 1:n_groups) {
  # HR and CI on one line
  text(x_max * 0.98, y_pos[i] + 0.15,
       sprintf("HR = %.2f (%.2f - %.2f)", hrs[i], lower[i], upper[i]),
       pos=2, cex=1.4, font=2)

  # P-value on second line
  text(x_max * 0.98, y_pos[i] - 0.15,
       sprintf("p = %.3e", pvals[i]),
       pos=2, cex=1.3)
}

# Add grid
grid(nx=NULL, ny=NA, col="gray90")

dev.off()
cat("Cox model forest plot saved to:", paste0("./cox_survival_", GENE, ".pdf\n"))
```

## Kaplan-Meier Survival Curves

```{r}
fit <- survfit(Surv(OS_MONTHS, OS_STATUS) ~ group, data = df)

# Colors matching sample (edit as desired)
curve_colors <- c("darkseagreen", "firebrick4", "deepskyblue1", "deeppink1")
legend_labels <- c("no_mutation", paste0(GENE, "_mut"), "LLM_benign", "LLM_oncogenic")

# Calculate log-rank p-value for display
logrank_pval <- pchisq(logrank_test$chisq,
                       length(logrank_test$n) - 1,
                       lower.tail = FALSE)

pdf(paste0("./km_survival_", GENE, ".pdf"), width=10, height=12)

# Try ggsurvplot first, fall back to base R if it fails
plot_success <- FALSE
if (survminer_available) {
  tryCatch({
    print(ggsurvplot(
      fit,
      data = df,
      risk.table = TRUE,
      pval = TRUE,  # Show p-value on plot
      pval.method = TRUE,  # Show test method
      pval.coord = c(0, 0.15),  # Position of p-value
      pval.size = 6,  # Larger p-value text
      conf.int = FALSE,
      risk.table.height = 0.3,
      legend.labs = legend_labels,
      legend.title = "",
      palette = curve_colors,
      xlab = "Months",
      ylab = "Survival probability",
      surv.scale = "percent",
      break.time.by = 20,
      risk.table.y.text.col = TRUE,
      risk.table.y.text = FALSE,
      font.main = c(18, "bold"),
      font.x = c(16, "bold"),
      font.y = c(16, "bold"),
      font.tickslab = c(14, "plain"),
      font.legend = c(14, "plain"),
      risk.table.fontsize = 5
    ))
    plot_success <- TRUE
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("ggsurvplot failed:", e$message, "\nUsing base R plotting instead.\n")
  })
}

# Fall back to base R plotting if ggsurvplot failed
if (!plot_success) {
  # Set up layout for main plot and risk table
  layout(matrix(c(1, 2), nrow = 2), heights = c(7, 3))

  # Main survival plot with larger fonts
  par(mar = c(5, 5, 4, 2))
  plot(fit,
       col = curve_colors,
       lwd = 3.5,
       xlab = "Months",
       ylab = "Survival probability",
       main = paste("Kaplan-Meier Survival Curves -", GENE),
       mark.time = TRUE,
       ylim = c(0, 1),
       cex.lab = 1.8,
       cex.main = 2.0,
       cex.axis = 1.6)

  # Add legend with larger font
  legend("topright",
         legend = legend_labels,
         col = curve_colors,
         lwd = 3.5,
         bty = "n",
         cex = 1.4)

  # Add log-rank test results in a box at bottom left
  # Create a nice formatted text box
  text_x <- max(fit$time) * 0.02
  text_y <- 0.15

  # Add background box
  rect(text_x - 2, text_y - 0.08, text_x + 40, text_y + 0.08,
       col = "white", border = "black", lwd = 2)

  # Add text with larger fonts
  text(text_x, text_y + 0.03,
       "Log-rank test",
       pos = 4, cex = 1.4, font = 2)
  text(text_x, text_y - 0.03,
       sprintf("p = %.3e", logrank_pval),
       pos = 4, cex = 1.3)

  # Risk table with larger fonts
  par(mar = c(5, 5, 0, 2))
  time_points <- seq(0, max(fit$time), by = 20)
  risk_summary <- summary(fit, times = time_points)

  plot(1, type = "n", xlim = range(time_points), ylim = c(0.5, length(unique(df$group)) + 0.5),
       xlab = "Months", ylab = "", yaxt = "n", main = "",
       cex.lab = 1.6, cex.axis = 1.4)

  for (i in 1:length(unique(df$group))) {
    idx <- risk_summary$strata == levels(df$group)[i]
    if (any(idx)) {
      text(time_points, rep(i, length(time_points)),
           risk_summary$n.risk[idx],
           col = curve_colors[i],
           cex = 1.2)
    }
  }

  axis(2, at = 1:length(legend_labels), labels = legend_labels, las = 1, cex.axis = 1.3)
  title(ylab = "Number at risk", line = 3.5, cex.lab = 1.6)
}

dev.off()
cat("KM survival plot saved to:", paste0("./km_survival_", GENE, ".pdf\n"))
```
